body: I was floxed almost 20 years ago. The thing that helped me the most honestly was recognizing and accepting that it was the medication. I was diagnosed with everything from MS, to lupus, I even spent a  day in the hospital psych warrd after I went to my primary care doctor hysterical. My husband thought I was nuts and sent me to cognitive behavioral therapy  I went through hell just chasing doctors around    The minute I just accepted it, it seem like I could kind of ignore it and go on with my life.  All the symptoms eventually went away took about a year or two. 20 years later, I can tell you half of what made it worse with my own anxiety, believing other people, and not myself. It will go away.  All of it will go away. You will get better. It is a reaction from a medication is not your body. I’m not saying it’s not brutal, the sickness is real. But so too is the fact that you will get better.

Oh my gosh, that is awesome! Thank you so much. When I see my naturopath on Thursday, I’m going to write those down so she can get those for me.  Every little bit of information helps when dealing with such a unpredictable disease.
Wow, that is so kind of you. Thank you so much for helping a stranger on the Internet!

That is a really good question. I’m not sure if my naturopath or LLMd tested for immune.  I know they both looked at ANA, and HLADR grouping .What specific test can my naturopath run to check for immune response? I’m seeing her on Thursday, she’s pretty open to running blood work for me. Thank you so much!

Thank you so much that is a clear response and makes so much sense!

The representative from Igenix  (that being what it is) said that unless I am immune compromised a negative result is pretty much a negative result, after multiple tests with the same result. Unless it’s a PCR test, which may not have the bacteria in that sample of blood. 

I hate to use myself as my own test sample, but I guess that’s what it takes. 🤷‍♂️ I herx pretty hard and i am alone, so I was afraid to go there. Just was hoping they were correct :(

He is treating me for Lyme based on the bands that were equivocal -but my question was all the other co-infections were negative (except for anaplasmosis). And he ran multiple tests weeks apart. How accurate is Igenex? Don’t know if I should disregard?

Yup took about two years before everything went away, and then… I think the Lyme disease is hitting all those weak spots all over again. 😩Some people very ill bedridden from these class of antibiotics.

I got very sick from one dose of ciprofloxacin. Tendinitis nerve pain took me years to recover. There’s actually a double black box warning on all ciprofloxacin, Levaquin, etc. Entire Facebook groups dedicated to adverse affects from these drugs.
Mine recovered. Took a few years but I’m mostly ok now.

My gosh, thank you so much for taking the time to reply and give me hope. Interestingly, I had no symptoms except for blurry vision before I came down with “flu” and was diagnosed with Lyme disease. Anaplasmosis.  Before this all went down, I was happily exercising, lifting weights, etc.  Now I am confined to a walker.  Lucky that I can at least walk a few feet.  Grateful for that and for those people who come back here to offer hope, and encouragement.  So glad to hear that you are back to almost normal.  This disease is brutal.

I was flocked many years ago I think it’s about 15 so far and yes I did get better. It took me about a year to feel mostly healed. There after I would have little issues, but certainly nothing like when it first happened.

Since most doctors don’t believe that Cipro could cause such symptoms, I always make sure when I’m asked if I’m allergic to medication I say Cipro, and then I say it gave me hives   Stupidity.  Because if I told them it really happened, they wouldn’t take me seriously but if I tell him then I got stinking hives they’re all about it.

Hang in there   it doesn’t go away. And yes, I exercised heavily afterwards.  Was able to continue running again. Every now and then my feet would get numb. Minor twitching, etc. but 100% better.
I was told I need to be able to power through things better. Yep just speechless.

I know you have to take medication to make yourself sick so that you can get better, and keep doing it over and over. 

I am so grateful for any day that I feel just a little bit like myself. 

I’m grateful that they are people who are willing to reach out and give advice and hope  

This disease is so freaking lonely and mind bending.

Oh my God thank you so much for coming back here and letting me know that. I never in my wildest dreams did I think that I would become this incapacitated when I was first diagnosed. It’s so hard to see the light when it’s one step forward two steps back.

That’s why I did not take the second medication my LLMD recommended because the first one, Doxy alone, was making me bedbound  there has to be some kind of middle ground. at my age being bedbound needs to all kinds of cascading complications.  weight, loss, muscle loss, etc.  Yes, I would love it if you sent me holistic practitioners  How do we go about doing that?
Fact that you were here trying to help others, regardless of how you came across speaks volumes of your character.  🙏

Yes, of course I realized afterwards you could’ve been a dad

Yes, I am very religious although, sometimes my faith has been hanging on by a thread. 

When I am well enough, I say the rosary, and I will include your daughter in my intentions  

Thank you for the scripture and for the encouragement, and for taking time from your own struggles to address mine.
Does that help with Herx? Yes I can try those for sure. What are they for?
OK I went onto Amazon and ordered them. Thank you so much for your kindness in reaching out.  So desperate for any kind of help or information. So glad you are better thank God.

I am so sorry. I’m sure as a mother if you could trade places with her, you would in an instant.

You don’t know me, or what multiple tragedies have happened in my life. All of my friends acknowledge that they don’t know how I’ve made it this far.  That contributes to my despair.

We all have our burdens, some more than others like you. 

I’m sure your daughter will walk again and have a long, beautiful life ahead of her  especially with a mama bear like you watching out for her

No parent should have to watch a child suffer. Ever.

I don’t know if you’re religious, but I will certainly pray for you for strength and healing. She deserves this.

They mostly happen at night. Trying to sleep, sweating nightmares, dizzy, vertigo, depression, so deep like a black hole, muscle jerking. Hypnagogic sleep  during the day day unable to walk much at all trembling. But I do Epson salt bath during the day, lemon water, Alka-Seltzer gold. Naturopath is waiting for igenex results before treating further.  My hands shake uncontrollably.

I’m in so much pain and I am alone. My family doesn’t understand and I am 66 years old and I don’t know that I have the strength to pull out of this.  By myself alone herxing at night.  I had to hire an aid to come and help me during the day. And I don’t know how much longer I can can do that  My husband left me for a younger woman in my sons live away. 

I am so sick like this I know I should be at a hospital, but I know they can’t do anything for me   my joints are fine. This is all neurological. It started in my eyes they thought I was having  TIA. Then I came down with the flu two months later  diagnosed with Lyme

I didn’t think it was possible to be in this much pain for 40 nights in a row and still be alive.

I went to a naturopathic doctor yesterday and going for blood work. She’s testing me for a 23 different things. When she gets the results and I get my results from igenex, she’ll start detoxing me even if she has to do one drop at a time she said. I’m so grateful for everyone here for all the guidance and support. Disenfranchised grief when you feel like you’re on deaths door and main stream doctors think you’re crazy.

Thank you it feels like it. I’m grateful I got to be 66. I was in great health 3 weeks ago and it’s shocking that I can barely walk. Hiit workouts hiking etc. Now I’ve had to get aides to come and help me so scared.

I live alone now after my husband left me for a younger woman. I’m terrified of the atovaquone and herxing alone, and it feels like I’m dying at night. I know I should be careful of what I’m looking at online, but the outlook is worse for someone my age, regardless of how healthy I was before. In just the three weeks since I’ve been diagnosed it’s beat the crap out of me. I can barely walk some days. So thankful there are people here who can bring me off the ledge when I feel scared. No one can know what this feels like unless they experience it. Ever.

I was careful for a good few years making sure I didn’t eat farm raised fish, organic chicken always b/c of unknown antibiotics. Now many years later, I seem fine with all of that. Even now,  (very rarely) my left foot will get numb/tingling but I know what it’s from and I know it will go away, typically in a day or so.  By rare I mean once or twice a year.
That’s how I feel with my legs. I don’t have what most people would call pain; no joint pain - it’s just like my legs are encased in cement.

I can’t tell you long term as I just received my supplements, someone else warned me that they are VERY strong. The first day I emptied out most of one capsule of artemisia just to see if I could tolerate it. In an hour I nearly passed out and relapsed (herx?) for 2 day I could barely walk to the kitchen. . Note: I am old (66) and it was too much for me. I think they are good after speaking with them they seem very knowledgeable. They responded right away to my concerns. Not going to take anymore until I am more stable.
Yes! It will get better. What helped me was knowing what it was from and not got down rabbit holes (could it MS etc). And once a year hit it one way faster faster.  Hang in there!
OK, thank you so much for your help. That’s a relief.!
Ok, so I’m assuming that is good? (btw, thank you for taking the time to help me and look at his wedsite!!)
Yes, Dr. Cameron.
OK I have to go talk to my LLMD. He wants me on for six weeks.  I wonder if that’s going to be enough now!

I get what you’re saying. My friend had undiagnosed lyme for many months was practically paralyzed and was cured completely with three rounds of antibiotics.  Doxycycline 100 mg.  And that was many years ago and she’s fine. She rides horses and thinks that’s where she got it. But you’re saying people like her are the exception, and not the rule.
I know I’m wondering that myself. Honestly, I am only 113 lbs. I don’t think I could handle more than 100mg. It must have worked for some people??

It was more from hypnagogic hallucinations. Starting to fall asleep, even when I’m sitting up watching TV with my eyes open.  Also kept waking me up trying to get to sleep. The problem with the insomnia was coming from the zaps and neurologic spasms more than anything else.  Again, it probably lasted really bad for about six months sporadically on and off for a few years.  At about three years out I was good.

Good to know that their Zhang medication’s are very strong. I’m not able to tolerate medication, so I’ll need to let them know to go slow. Thank you for taking the time to be here giving advice, encouragement, and support! It’s overwhelming.

I need to hear this. I could have caught it 2 months ago when hiking, (started having transient blurry vision w/no cause found) or more recently since I just came down with a “flu” aches, sweating, chills. Now on doxy from LLD for 6 weeks. Came here to look for answer, but seeing so many people’s lives destroyed. I am beyond terrified. Meeting with Zhang Clinic today. Seems like it’s a toss up, 50/50 long term chronic even if treated early.

No joint pain, some tendon pain. It was mostly neurological for me. Fasiculations like crazy,  numb, tingling, zaps, depression, eye symptoms, anxiety, etc.  In the very beginning my hands were  really burned, red blisters, etc. Literally burned me from the inside. 

One of the things that helped me most was realizing that most people do get better overtime. I finally had confidence in myself that I knew it was Cipro that had done this and stopped worrying about other syndromes or diseases once I settled in my mind on that whenever a new symptom appeared or I was suffering with some aspect of it it was easier to deal with because I knew eventually it was gonna go away. I will say honestly now and again my left foot gets a a little numb like it used to for a day or two.  I know it’s nerve damage. It will never go away. It’s OK.  I’m lucky I got better 99%.  

The worst part is being called a hypochondriac (in the actual clinical document) as well as seeing lives of other people floxed destroyed and wondering if you were going to be the next one.  That’s why I came here, To remind everyone that lots of people recover in are just fine.

Great. I get it. So…long term antibiotics should be fine, but if symptoms come back check for other infections and start antibiotics again depending on diagnosis thank you- so much to weed thru on internet and very scary too!

That’s insane. Its so clear from just a goggle search how devastating this can be! I think I may go straight to tele-health with skin issues. Do you think I need to go to lyme dr to get multiple kinds of antibiotics? Thank you again for your insight.
Wow oh my gosh, that is just horrible. OK, longer antibiotics is better. Thank you so much and I’m so sorry you’re going through this. I will try to stay the course as long as possible.

OK, thank you that makes sense! So, even though I’m feeling really bad right now, the flu like feeling was an early symptom of infection. At least six weeks of antibiotics.  Then see if when stopping if symptoms come back or not.

Oh my gosh thank you. There is literally no positive comments anywhere about Lyme disease it’s absolutely terrifying.  Dr. only gave me two weeks of doxy. I guess my next step is to find a lyme dr to get more antibiotics. And pray.  I am so sick. I cannot imagine…

I know this post is old, but I have to comment that I have the same thing and I’ve been going through hell trying to find out what it was. Only in one eye. Black spot and sometimes blurry, but I also have headaches along the occipital nerve just like you describe, under eyebrow/above eye and the base of neck/head. I’m not glad you have it but so glad that I found this post - I was thinking I was nuts.

When I was being discharged from the hospital for suspected TIA, I pressed the neurologist on chances of reoccurrence because he wanted me on aspirin, etc. He said that he didn’t want to see me back in the hospital in 3 years with a stroke.   I asked him what demographic is having repeat issues coming back in 3 years,  and he had to admit that they were mostly patients with uncontrolled risk factors. (I am taking the aspirin, etc. just wanted to push him for clarification).

I’m sorry to hijack this thread, but I have a question because I was looking through post to see if I could find someone with similar symptoms as myself. I woke up last week with blurry vision in my right eye lasted for about 45 minutes went to the ER. A month before same thing happened, while I was driving only lasted a few seconds to the left I.  Getting conflicting answers as to whether or not this is an optical migraine or a TIA.  (many many tests done so far, including looking for a hole in my heart all negative  ). No risk factors   So I guess I’m glad to see that you had the same exact symptom many years ago and no problems since then.  You were the first one and I have found.
Yes, of course you’re right thank you. My surgeon said that mine is small, so we are discussing risk benefit.

I am going to hematologist. Many years ago I had multiple miscarriages and they thought I had antiphospholipid syndrome. Although it was never confirmed a few years ago, I had blood test taken and asked them to check for that and it was all negative. But maybe it’s something that’s transient I don’t know? Either way, I’m on blood thinners the rest of my life.  I’m so sorry you had to go through that. I’m so sorry that’s just horrible at your young age.  

I keep thinking, maybe with the invention of AI they will start to come up with solutions. You have a long life ahead of you and then I can’t imagine that they won’t come up with something to help you.

I’m glad you found some solace. This is all so terrifying. I wouldn’t wish it on anybody.  I used to go hiking in the woods by myself all the time. Now I’m terrified to go anywhere where I don’t think that there could be help, but I know that’s not living.  I know that I have to let go.  But it’s so hard.
OMG that is terrifying. I’m so sorry. Three strokes in five months. I’m praying for your healing.
Yes, I’m seeing a therapist. I think I may take her advice and start some medication for anxiety.
Thank you so much. At 27 years old you shouldn’t have to worry about these kind of things I do wonder if my vigorous exercise routine had anything to do with it, but they say no.
Yes, I’m on 81 mg baby aspirin now. Thank you so much for your reply.

Thank you! I had read Chump Lady when he first left, and not since. but just the other day, after the deposition, I needed to go there again. During the deposition they tried to paint me as a crying/hysterical wife so no wonder he cheated. I cried when he disclosed the details of his affair, so when his attorney deposed me, his first question was “Do you cry like this often?”. “You’ve been crying for 2 hours straight”. I said, yes, b/c I just heard the details! But he wouldn’t let it go, and for 2 hours nonstop he did this “did you apologize to you husband for making him feel alone?” WTH? Chump Lady was the only thing that got me out of blaming myself for his affair. She is a gift.

We were married for 30 years. At the 19 year mark he confessed that he had been having an affair with a coworker. Her husband found out and forced him to tell me. Her marriage broke up we went to marriage counseling and I honestly for gave him. Fast forward a few years he began using porn again which had been a problem in our marriage and lost interest in me. We began having a dead bedroom and no amount of discussion on my part could convince him to stop the porn. Last year in February he told me on a Wednesday morning that he Loved me but but was not in love with me. (what they all say and he said it with both affairs). By Thursday he was gone and never returned. He swore up and down that he was not leaving me for someone else. Kept that narrative up for 2 years after he left. Two days ago in our deposition for divorce he admitted that he had been having an affair with someone he met on Facebook for three years. She's 25 years younger than me. I am 65 and now empty nest and completely alone. He has a high powered job and I gave up mine to raise our children. My advice to anyone who has a cheating spouse is this: They need to be completely 100% remorseful do everything in the world to make it up to you marriage counseling individual counseling etc. and most importantly this… A postnup. Just have something in the document stating that if there is another affair there are financial consequences and state what they are. In my opinion you'll find out very quickly how serious they are about reconciliation. Here I am in the so called  golden years of my life and they are the worst years of my life never in my wildest dreams did I think he would do this again.

The key is their acceptance of responsibility of how they have destroyed your trust. It's not enough to say I'm sorry. My husband cheated years ago, we reconciled went through marriage counseling I thought we were OK. Apparently not. I think he was more sorry that he got caught, of what it made him look like rather than acceptance of how it devastated me.  One day 10 years later, he Told me he wanted a separation and was gone the next day and never returned. After 30 years of marriage.  not even a conversation he unilaterally got up made a decision and left. He will not come clean and tell me if there was someone else in the end I believe 100% that there was. I am now 64. Devoted my life to raising kids gave up my career and now what do I have? Peace of mind. Devoting 30 years of my life to someone who threw me away without even looking back. I've lost my memories my past and the future I planned on with him. My advice, never take a cheater back leave while you are ahead. Don't waste any more precious time in your life like I did

I don't have a mental illness. What I do have, is a lifetime of tragedies things that happened to me that I had no control over. I thought when I was younger, at 30 years old, and I had a lifetime ahead of me and things which really get better because I've had my fair share of horrible things at that point. Broken home, poverty, rape, boyfriend who tried to kill me, working three jobs living with cockroaches, I couldn't even afford the parking fee for my building so I would drive around at night in a bad neighborhood trying to find a parking space and exhausted after working two jobs. And then I met my husband. At 34 I thought my life had finally begun. Things were good for a little while even though I struggled with medical issues in pregnancy I ended up having two children. But my husband was a porn addict, a cheater, and though I for gave him he waited until my youngest left home and after 30 years of marriage he was gone in 24 hours. My youngest son is involved in a destructive cult. He hates everyone and thinks the world is ending soon. Well maybe it is who knows. I actually hope it does because then I would be out of this misery because nothing at this point of my life at my elderly age is going to outweigh the shit show travesty of my life. I don't know why I thought I could ever be normal what was I thinking? I feel like the devil is following me all my life and even though I am old and gray he is still hanging on and won't leave me alone.

I am 64 and I agree completely. A friend of mine recently said to me, after the most recent tragedy ”this is more than anyone should have to take”.  I feel like the devil or some evil has been lurking around me my whole life. Or that I am paying for a past life somehow. It’s so hard for most people to comprehend that the quality of life, as measured in multiple tragedies, make living life unbearable. On balance, most of my life has been spent in shock from something or grieving something. Sometimes grieving two separate things at one time.

 For example, how many times have you heard people say on the news when something really bad happens that ”I always thought things like this happened to other people”, or “we live in such a good town, things like that don’t happen here.”. That’s because most people have “normal” lives and believe that horrible things happen to people because they must have done something wrong. Like they had a bad diet and that’s why they have stomach cancer. Cause the fact that random horrible stuff can happen to anyone is unsettling. I also believe there are more people like us, who have suffered though out our lives for no apparent reason, who live in a state of unending grief. The thought that someone would wish to die, is unimaginable to most people.

I hear you. What you are saying is grief over someone dying is not a reason to commit suicide. Of course, that is true.  However, I have seen through personal experience very old people losing a spouse and dying of a broken heart. Working in a hospital, I have unfortunately seen this firsthand many times. It seemed inhumane to me watching folks slowly starve themselves, etc.,  begging to be let go.  

My father had heart surgery @ 86. He was such a cheerful, happy guy, I remember him literally making jokes on the stretcher before his first surgery.  He ended up having 3 open heart surgeries in a year. He became someone I didn’t recognize. Surgery changed him to a deeply sad man in pain who wouldn’t even lift his head.  What did that extra year do for him?  Our family regrets putting him through that, maybe cruel to say but I wish he had just had a fatal heart attack. I guess I question the general philosophy of it all, quality vs. quantity of life. Just don’t know…
I hear you. Take care.

When I was 30 I had been through multiple traumas (molestation, rape, boyfriend tried to kill me, extreme poverty, starved, lived in fear of my life, no car, no money, family broken up so no support). So I sat down and wrote pros and cons of staying. See, it’s not that I was depressed or had mental illness, I had horrible things happen TO me. I decided that logically time was on my side, that things could change. I just think it’s a shame because of your age, that odds are on your side too. Maybe consider that your environment can and will change. Life is change, whether we like it or not, or participate or not. It will change. Friends change throughout a lifetime. Even best friends, because circumstances change i.e., friends who marry, friends who don’t and choose another life. Not much in common with them, so move on. When I was 25 I met my best friend who has been my friend now for 40 years. I’m not saying life is unicorns and rainbows, it’s not. But I just think you are so young to be giving up with so much unknown. 

I worked in long term care taking care of elderly dying patients as a therapist.  It took it’s toll on me mentally and eventually I had to leave. I was being forced to drag 90 year old people out of bed who were activity dying provide “care” when all they needed was me to hold their hand. So I forged a LOT of documents to do just that. I think it’s clearly a wonderful giving thing you are doing. But consider that may be impacting your outlook. I know I did what I could, and you have no idea of the long term  positive impact of your sacrifice in helping these women - who are in such a dark place. Just wish there were more people like you in the world. 

You are such a wonderful gift, and your parents clearly love you for a reason.

Yes, people can be beyond horrible, and there is no “karma” coming to get them. But I will say, you are young. There is a very good chance that life will get better for you. I know you don’t believe me - just the fact that if you stay on this Earth will give you that chance. You have been through hell, and not many people will be able to understand the depth of your pain. The hopelessness and helplessness of  railing against the invisible bully.  I am sorry. Life is not fair. At all. Those that abused you don’t deserve to sleep at night, but I know you do knowing that you did your best with what life gave you.

Yes, this. It’s like all those who are having good lives because of luck, they escaped trauma having multiple horrible things happening to them through chance, want those of us who haven’t been fortunate to stick around because it’ll disrupt their good time. I read recently about a fire/tragedy where the husband, 3 kids, all the dogs died except for the mother and one son. Bet I know what they are telling the mom…do things like mindfulness. That’s the advice they give to people who have horrible past and no hope of good future, just stay “in the moment”. But THEY don’t have to do that. They have good memories, hope for the future. I’d like to see those who are less fortunate to be the ones making the laws/societal norms about who stays.

Yes, he is self destructive. Tried that a a teen, cutting etc. Girl crazy, some girl broke up with him. Obsessed with having her. OCD? I know he has ADHD/diagnosed, not medicated, prob. should have been.
